# Findings — Notion as Code alpha

Feedback-tracker candidates, accumulated across builds. **Numbers are stable —
append, never renumber** (they get cited in feedback to Notion). Findings 1–7
come from the **knoxx-rnd** deploy (2026-07-24); 8–16 from modelling the live
**crm** build as code; 21–24 from **setup-core** and **default-teamspace-probe** in the demo workspace;
25–28 from rechecking the DSL that `ntn` 0.23.20 ships (**dsl-recheck-probe**); 29 from
**template-demo**, the first build generated by the core template.

## Bugs and hard limits (1–6)

1. **🐛 Cross-data-source formula references are mis-bound.** A Formulas 2.0
   expression `prop("relation").map(current.prop("related-prop")).sum()` is
   accepted, and both property IDs resolve — but the rewriter binds the inner
   property token to the *current* data source's collection ID instead of the
   related one, so the formula silently evaluates to 0. Verified via
   `GET /v1/data_sources/{id}`: the rewritten expression carries the wrong
   collection ID on the inner `block_property` token. (Same-data-source formula
   references, e.g. Activities' `Eligible Hours`, work correctly.)
2. **No conditional rollups** — "sum of Hours where Grant Eligible = Yes" can't
   be expressed: rollups don't filter, and Notion as Code rollups can't target
   formula properties (`RollupTargetPropertyType` excludes `formula`). Combined
   with finding 1, a grant-hours-per-project number currently requires a manual
   UI formula. Workaround shipped in knoxx-rnd: an `Eligible Hours` formula on
   Activities + the filtered **ATO Activities** view.
3. **Non-TTY runs silently cancel** — the first-run confirmation prompt returns
   `""` when stdin isn't a TTY, so agent/CI runs abort. Workaround: always pass
   `--sessionStateFilePath`, which is what `npm run build` does.
4. **No relative-date view filters** — fixed `YYYY-MM-DD` only, so "Today's
   Activities" / "Today's Meetings" can't be built as specced; both builds fall
   back to date-sorted lists.
   **Recheck 2026-10-16: confirmed fixed for presets.** A `date_is` +
   `today` filter deploys and reads back (as a quick filter, finding 21).
   `relative_to_today` ranges ("next 2 weeks", "this month") are accepted but
   read back `null`, so they're unconfirmed until a UI check (finding 25).
5. **Person property values can't be set by script** — columns exist, seed rows
   leave them empty. Teamspace membership also can't be configured.
6. **Auto-increment ID prefixes are workspace-global** — `KIP`/`KIA`/`KIK`/`KIC`
   (knoxx-rnd) and `CRMC`/`CRMD` (crm) must not collide with each other or with
   any existing database in the workspace. Tracked in
   [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) and enforced by `npm run check`.

## Feature request (7)

7. **✨ Permissions-as-code.** No intent exists for teamspace membership/roles,
   database share levels, or locking (a `TeamspaceMember` type is declared in
   `types.ts` but nothing accepts it — likely roadmap). Scripts can't prevent
   UI-side schema edits, so every deploy target needs a manual permissioning
   pass (see each build's NOTES.md). Declared schema + locked schema would make
   one-way push safe by construction — the natural complement to there being no
   pull or drift detection — and is what governance-heavy builds (e.g. an ATO
   evidence system) actually need. Also erodes the "same script, many
   workspaces" story until it exists.

## Gaps found modelling a live production workspace (8–15)

Expressing a real workspace as code surfaced a different class of gap — less
"this is buggy", more "this whole surface isn't in the DSL yet". Of the CRM's 87
views, roughly a third cannot be expressed at all.

8. **No chart or dashboard view types.** `ViewType` is table | board | calendar
   | list | gallery | feed | timeline. The CRM's 7 charts (Deal Value by
   Stage/Owner, Open Deals by Stage/Owner, Contacts Created, Contacts by
   Source/Owner) and its "Contact Dashboard" have no representation. Charts are
   how the CRM is actually *read* — the largest single gap. Curiously `feed` is
   creatable but not readable: `GET /v1/views/{id}` 400s with
   `Unsupported view type: feed`.
9. **No buttons, and no database automations at all.** The intent union is
   exactly `space | teamspace | database | page | view | file_attachment |
   custom_agent`; `automation`, `trigger`, `webhook` and `button` appear nowhere
   in the DSL. Nor is there an out-of-band route: the public REST API has no
   automation endpoint (every shape of `/v1/automations` returns 400
   `invalid_request_url`) and data-source retrieve omits them, so automations
   can't even be read back for comparison. A scripted build is therefore
   structure-and-read-only by construction — the CRM's whole write path
   (Register Lead, Create Xero Contact, Create Slack Channel, Create Google
   Drive Folder, Enrich, Add to Mailing List, Create Harvest Project) plus every
   database automation stays a manual post-deploy pass. Together with finding 7,
   this is what stops one script from fully provisioning a client workspace.
   **Recheck 2026-10-16: still open here.** Database automations are in the
   DSL (`addAutomation`, `create_page` only) and the server recognises them,
   but it rejected the run: "Database automations require a workspace on the
   Plus plan or higher." The Demo workspace is on Free, so untested beyond
   that. Buttons still have no DSL surface (finding 25).
10. **No `place` property type** (Companies → Address) — degrades to text.
11. **No number formats.** `number` takes no `format`, so `number_with_commas`
    (Deal Value) and `percent` (Probability) are lost; a percent property has to
    be hand-formatted after deploy.
12. **View filters can't express `is_empty` / `is_not_empty`.** The CRM's
    pipeline board means "open deals" as *Actual Close is empty*. Approximated
    with three `status_is_not` filters — which also probes whether multiple
    filters AND together (undocumented).
    **Recheck 2026-10-16: still open.** There's still no `is_empty` operator.
    Advanced `and` / `or` groups are **confirmed fixed**, and they deploy as
    the view's saved filter (finding 27).
13. **Rollups can't target `unique_id`** either (`RollupTargetPropertyType`
    excludes it, as it does `formula` — finding 2), so Deals → Company ID is
    unbuildable, as are Deals → Slack Channel / Google Drive Folder (formula
    targets).
14. **No tabs block** in page-content markdown, so the CRM hub's tabbed left
    column (Quick Actions / Databases) becomes callouts + columns.
    **Recheck 2026-10-16: confirmed fixed.** A `<tabs>` block with two
    `<tab>`s deploys as a `tab` block with two panes (finding 25).
15. **Date values are date-only.** `notion.date(start, end?)` compiles to a
    Notion inline date mention carrying only `start_date` / `end_date` — no
    `start_time`, no `time_zone` — so a calendar-synced database (meetings,
    emails) loses its times. Passing an ISO datetime just puts a malformed
    string into `start_date`.

## Feature request (16)

16. **✨ A pull / import path.** Reconstructing the CRM schema took ~90 API calls
    (databases → data sources → views list → each view) and a lot of manual
    transliteration into `types.ts` shapes; `tools/pull-schema.ts` in this repo
    automates the extraction but not the script generation.
    `notion-as-code pull <databaseId>` emitting a script would make the alpha
    usable on existing workspaces, not just greenfield ones — and would let
    scripts become the source of truth for builds that already exist, which is
    every client build worth governing.

## From the crm first deploy + re-deploy (17–19)

Deployed 2026-07-25. Run #1 created all 48 intents; run #2 re-ran the same
script with one schema change.

17. **One filter per property per view, enforced server-side.** Three stacked
    `status_is_not` filters on one view are rejected outright:
    `validation_error: Duplicate filter for property "dl-status". Each property
    can only have one filter per view.` So the finding-12 workaround for
    "Actual Close is empty" doesn't exist either — an open-pipeline view cannot
    be expressed at all. Useful side effect: **validation happens before any
    resource is created**, so a rejected run is atomic — the session file and
    workspace were untouched after the failure.
18. **🐛 A re-deploy silently clears dual-relation values on existing pages.**
    Run #2 was resource-idempotent — 63 mappings unchanged, no ID churn, 5 deal
    rows not 10 — and preserved every title, select, number, date, multi_select,
    formula, rollup config, unique_id and page content block. But **every
    dual-relation value written by run #1 came back empty**: deals ↔ contacts,
    deals ↔ meetings, deals ↔ emails, contacts ↔ companies, meetings/emails ↔
    companies, all zeroed. Two things survived and point at the cause: the
    **one-way** relation (Companies → Primary Billing Contact) kept its value,
    and so did the one-sided links described in finding 19. So a re-run appears
    to rewrite dual-relation page values as empty rather than leaving them
    alone — which makes re-deploying a populated workspace destructive to
    exactly the data that expresses the model. Evidence snapshot:
    `builds/crm/source/post-redeploy-relation-state.json`.
19. **🐛 A dual relation can land one-sided.** After the clean first deploy, the
    script's `Deals → Company` value (written on the deal) was readable from the
    **Companies** side (`Deals` populated, `No. Deals` = 1) but read empty from
    the **Deals** side, silently emptying the `Company Name` and `Domain`
    rollups that depend on it. Identically-shaped dual relations written on the
    same rows in the same run (`Contact`, `Meeting Notes`, `Emails`) read
    correctly from both sides, so it isn't the write itself. Dropping `limit: 1`
    from the property did not fix it — though that retest ran through run #2 and
    is confounded by finding 18, so `limit` is not cleanly ruled out.
    Feels related to finding 1: a paired property bound to the wrong collection
    would read exactly like this.

Also confirmed on these runs:

- **Multi-data-source databases work.** One `Core CRM Objects` database with
  three data sources (Contacts / Companies / Deals) deployed as specced.
- **Views-only linked databases work**, including several tabs per block:
  `notion.database()` with `dataSources` omitted produced the hub's Emails
  (2 tabs), Meetings (3), Deals (2) and Contacts (2) blocks.
- **Self-referencing dual relations work** — Contacts → `Duplicate of` /
  `Duplicated by` resolved to the same data source with correct pairing.
- **Forward page references in relation values work** — Fernbrook's
  `Primary Billing Contact` resolved to a contact page created later in the
  script.
- **Board `columns` group hiding is accepted but has no effect.** The three
  hidden status groups came back as `groups: None` in the view configuration;
  the board shows every column.
- **Finding 1 reproduces on a second formula shape.** Contacts' `Latest
  Meeting` / `Latest Email` use `map`/`filter`/`sort`/`last` rather than `sum`;
  the deployed expressions reference only their own collection ID, and all rows
  evaluate empty. Same-data-source formulas were all correct (Meeting `Status`
  → Upcoming/Completed, Deal `Expected Value` = 33 600, Company Slack/Drive
  URL builders).
- **Auto-increment prefixes, status groups and rollups otherwise work**:
  `CRMC-1`, `CRMD-1…5`, the full Lead → Closed status set with its three
  groups, and the Meetings → `Company Names` rollup.
- **`me` person filters are unverifiable via the API** — `GET /v1/views/{id}`
  returns `filter: null` for the My Emails / My Meetings views (the finding
  documented under "reading a build back out"), so whether they deployed
  correctly can only be confirmed in the UI.

## From the crm re-deploy of 2026-10-08 (20)

20. **🐛 `<mention-database>` is now rejected server-side.** Re-deploying the
    unchanged crm script failed with `internal_server_error: Unsupported tag
    <mention-database> in Notion as Code. Replace it with a supported Markdown
    tag.` The same three hub-page mentions deployed fine on 2026-07-25, and the
    SDK branch (`notion-sdk-js` @ `3d33935`, 2026-07-23, which predates that
    deploy) still lists `<mention-database>` as supported in
    `INFRA_AS_CODE_MARKDOWN_SPEC`. So the server changed and the published spec
    didn't. The rejection is atomic (as in finding 17): the session file was
    untouched. Local `check` / `typecheck` can't catch it, since it's
    server-side. Workaround shipped in crm and knoxx-rnd: plain bold database
    names instead of mention chips. Untested: whether `<mention-page>`,
    `<mention-data-source>` and `<mention-agent>` are rejected too.

## From the setup-core and default-teamspace-probe deploys of 2026-10-16 (21–24)

First build in the workFlowers Demo workspace. One run created 69 resources and 27
properties, no errors.

21. **View `filters` deploy as quick filters, not as the view's saved filter.**
    `GET /v1/views/{id}` returns `filter: null` with the script's filter under
    `quick_filters` instead (e.g. `{"select": {"equals": ["Operations"]}}`). The
    crm `Closed Won` view from 2026-07-25 reads back the same way, so this isn't
    new server behaviour, just newly noticed. The rows are still filtered, but
    as a removable pill in the filter bar, so any viewer can clear it. It also
    corrects the "reading a build back out" caveat below: a `null` filter
    doesn't only mean a relative-date or `me` filter. The DSL has no way to ask
    for a saved (locked) filter.
22. **Finding 19 reproduces on a clean first deploy.** All 6 `Tasks → Project`
    values read empty from the Tasks side, while `Projects → Tasks` shows the
    right counts (2 / 1 / 3) and the schema pairs correctly (`dual_property`,
    synced IDs match both ways). `Meeting Notes → Project` and `Docs → Project`,
    written the same way in the same run with the same `limit: 1`, read
    correctly from both sides, and the compiled intents for the three are
    identical in shape. With no re-deploy involved, finding 18 is ruled out as
    the cause. One structural difference: every task row is also the target of
    the one-way `Meeting Notes → Action Items` relation. That's untested as the
    cause, and crm's one-sided `Deals → Company` had no one-way relation
    pointing at Deals.

23. **✅ A script can create the all-company default teamspace, alongside the
    one the workspace ships with.** A teamspace created with
    `accessLevel: "default"` shows as **Default** in Settings → Teamspaces,
    even though the workspace already has the default teamspace Notion
    pre-installs. Notion keeps both as defaults, with no conflict and no
    error. The script can't remove or demote the pre-installed one, because it
    can only reference resources it creates, but an admin can delete it by hand
    if it's empty. So a provisioning script *can* own the all-company
    teamspace, and the cleanup is one manual step.
24. **A re-deploy silently ignores a teamspace access-level change.** A
    teamspace created `open` and re-deployed with `accessLevel: "default"`
    still shows **Open**. The run succeeded, reported nothing, and left every
    mapping unchanged. So access level only applies on create: choose
    `default` on a teamspace's first deploy, or change it by hand and update
    the script to match. It's unclear whether other teamspace fields (name,
    icon, description) update on re-deploy.

Also confirmed on this run:

- **One script can create several teamspaces at different access levels.**
  Company (`open`), Operations and Marketing (`closed`) all came from one
  deploy. The access levels aren't readable through the public API (pages
  report `parent: workspace`, and Notion's hosted MCP returns 403 for a
  personal access token), so they can only be confirmed in the UI.
- **A teamspace can hold a linked view of a database in another teamspace.**
  Each team page's views-only database has a view whose `data_source_id` is
  the Company data source, filtered to that team (as a quick filter, finding
  21).
- **A database can live inside a page in a non-private teamspace.** Vendors
  is a child of the Operations Home page.
- **`<mention-page>` is still accepted.** That answers part of the finding-20
  open question. Both Home pages render their chips as `page` mentions.
- **One-way relations write fine.** `Action Items` (Meeting Notes → Tasks)
  holds 2 / 1 / 2 values as written.

## Rechecking the DSL that `ntn` 0.23.20 ships, 2026-10-16 (25–28)

25. **The SDK branch is frozen; the current DSL ships with `ntn`.**
    `EXPERIMENTAL__notion-as-code` on makenotion/notion-sdk-js is still at
    `3d33935` (2026-07-23). The current DSL is the one `ntn notion-as-code new`
    downloads: makenotion/notion-as-code-template @ `80be619` (2026-10-06),
    whose `src/lib/types.d.ts` says it is vendored from a newer SDK runtime.
    `ntn` posts to `/v1/infra_as_code` with
    `Notion-Beta: notion-as-code-2026-07-31`, and its state file uses the same
    `resourceIdToPointerMappings` / `resourceIdToPropertyIdMappings` shape as our
    `session.json`. So this repo now has an `ntn` engine: a build with
    `"engine": "ntn"` compiles against `vendor/ntn-template` and deploys through
    `ntn notion-as-code apply --state <session.json>`, still via `npm run build`.
    Diffing the template's types against `3d33935`:

    | Finding | In the 2026-10-06 types | Verdict |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 4 relative-date filters | `date_is` + `{type: "relative", value: "today"}` (also tomorrow, yesterday, ±1 week, ±1 month); `date_is_relative_to` past / next / this N day–year; `date_is_within` exact ranges; `dateFilterMode: "end_date"` | fixed in the DSL |
    | 9 automations / buttons | `dataSource.addAutomation()` → `database_automation` intent: triggers `page_added`, `property_updated` (optionally per property), or a recurrence; one action type, `create_page` (optional template); Plus plan or higher. No button anywhere. | automations partly fixed; buttons still open |
    | 12 `is_empty` / advanced filters | no `is_empty` / `is_not_empty` operator (typecheck rejects it); new `{type: "advanced", operator: "and" \| "or", filters}` groups, nestable | `is_empty` still open; advanced filters fixed in the DSL |
    | 14 tabs | `<tab icon="…">` in `<tabs>` in the Markdown spec | fixed in the DSL |
    | feed views | `feed` was already a view type (finding 8); now adds `showAuthorByline` | unchanged in the DSL |
    | `this_page` per-record layouts | `pageLayout.tabs` takes `{type: "view", resourceId}` tabs; `relation_contains` accepts `{type: "relative", value: "this_page"}` | new |

    Other changes seen in the diff, not probed: `notion.datetime()` with times
    and time zone (finding 15's gap), `verification` properties, view `groupBy`
    for most property types, view icons, recurring templates and default
    templates, custom-agent triggers and access, and a rewritten Markdown spec.
    The spec now writes mentions as `<mention url="resourceId" type="database">`
    with bare resource IDs, not `<mention-database url="{{id}}">`, which may
    be why finding 20's tag is rejected.

    **Server results** ([dsl-recheck-probe](../builds/dsl-recheck-probe/NOTES.md),
    deployed 2026-10-16 on the fourth run, read back through the public API):

    | Finding | Server | Evidence |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 4 | ✅ presets; ranges unconfirmed | "Due today" reads `quick_filters: {Due: {date: {equals: "today"}}}`. "Next 2 weeks" and "Ends this month" read `filter: null, quick_filters: null`, the same as relative/`me` filters always have (see "Reading a build back out"), so only the UI can confirm them. |
    | 9 | ❌ on Free | run 3 rejected: "Database automations require a workspace on the Plus plan or higher." Nothing was created. |
    | 12 | `is_empty` ❌, advanced ✅ | "In progress or overdue" reads `filter: {or: [status equals In progress, Due before today]}`. "Open, due soon" reads `{and: [status ≠ Done, {or: [Due equals today]}]}`: its nested `relative_to_today` member is missing from the readback, unconfirmed as above. Two filters on one property inside an `or` group were accepted (cf. finding 17). |
    | 14 | ✅ | the hub's first block after the intro is a `tab` block whose two children are the "Overview" and "What to check" panes. |
    | feed views | created; still unreadable | `GET /v1/views/{id}` still returns 400 `Unsupported view type: feed`. |
    | `this_page` layouts | created; filter unconfirmed | the run mapped the page layout (`type: "layout"`), its content view and the tab view; the tab view reads `filter: null`. The page-layout content view 400s with `Unsupported view type: page`. |

    Runs 1 and 2 hit two new server rules, both rejected at validation with
    nothing created:

    - A view used as a page-layout tab must be declared on its own data
      source's database. Adding it to the Projects database gave `View
      "drp-project-tasks-tab-view" references unknown data source
      "drp-tasks-ds" in database "drp-projects-db".`
    - **A child database must be placed in its parent page's content.** It
      failed with `Child database "drp-projects-db" must appear exactly once as
      <database url="{{drp-projects-db}}"> in parent page "drp-hub" content.`
      Setup-core's databases have pages as parents too and deployed earlier the
      same day through the SDK runner, so the rule may only apply under the
      `ntn` beta header. Untested.

26. **`ntn` rewrites the state file in a new shape.** After the apply,
    `session.json` holds `resourceIdToResourcePointers` (each entry has `type`
    in place of `table`, and properties are included as `collection_property`
    entries with their `collectionId`) plus a `meta` block (`workspaceId`,
    `lastAppliedAtMs`, `lastScript`, `createdRecordCounts`). The
    `resourceIdToPointerMappings` / `resourceIdToPropertyIdMappings` keys are
    gone. The seed in the old shape was read correctly. `tools/builds.ts` now
    accepts both shapes for the anchor check. Untested: whether the SDK runner
    can read the new shape, so don't switch a build's engine back after an
    `ntn` deploy.
27. **Advanced filter groups deploy as the view's saved filter.** Single
    filters still land in `quick_filters` (finding 21, reconfirmed by "Due
    today"), but both views whose filter is an `and` / `or` group read back
    with it under `filter` and nothing in `quick_filters`. So wrapping a lone
    filter in a one-member `and` group may be the way to get a saved filter
    that viewers can't clear. That's untested on a one-member group.
28. **Plan-gated intents fail after submission, but still atomically.** The
    automation was rejected by the async task (`internal_server_error`), not
    at validation, but nothing was created and `session.json` was untouched,
    like the validation failures in findings 17 and 20.

## From the template-demo deploy of 2026-10-16 (29)

First build generated from a spec by the core template (TKT-978). One run
created 53 resources and 36 properties, no errors.

29. **A build script can't import another file.** The SDK copies the script's
    text into an async function in a temp directory and runs that with Node.
    A static `import` is then a syntax error, and `require` can't resolve a
    relative path or load a `.ts` file. Only dynamic imports of Node built-ins
    work. So a template can't be shared across builds as a module: this repo
    generates a self-contained `build.ts` per client instead
    (`npm run new-build`, see `templates/workspace-setup/README.md`).

Also confirmed on this run:

- **A multi-select team filter works.** `propertyType: "multi_select"`,
  `operator: "enum_contains"` reads back as
  `quick_filters: {"multi_select": {"contains": ["TD Operations"]}}`, so it's
  a quick filter like every script filter (finding 21). Querying with the same
  filter returns a task tagged with both teams for both teams, and an
  Operations-only task for Operations only.
- **Relations written through the public API pair correctly**, including
  `Tasks → Project`, the side that read empty in finding 22. Test rows
  created after the deploy read correctly from both sides, and `Action Items`
  stayed one-way. So the finding 19/22 problem is in how a script writes
  relation values, not in the relation schema it creates.
- **Timeline and calendar views deploy** from `timelineBy` and `calendarBy`
  (Projects Timeline, Meeting Notes Calendar).
- **"My" views can be scripted.** A person filter with
  `value: { type: "relative", value: "me" }` deploys (My projects, My tasks,
  My meetings), but it reads back `null` in both `filter` and `quick_filters`.
  So only the UI shows whether it landed, and whether as a saved filter or a
  quick filter (finding 21).
- **A re-deploy that only adds views is clean on an empty build.** The second
  template-demo run added 3 view mappings and changed none.
- **A re-deploy renames in place.** The third run renamed page titles and
  views, and renamed multi-select options without leaving the old ones
  behind, on an empty build. Whether it renames teamspaces (left open in
  finding 24) can only be checked in the UI.
- **A teamspace's top-level pages can be trashed through the public API**
  (`PATCH /v1/pages/{id}` with `in_trash: true`), which is how `setup-core`
  and `default-teamspace-probe` were removed. Teamspaces themselves can only be
  deleted in the UI. Child databases still read `in_trash: false` afterwards,
  so the flag isn't inherited in API reads.

## Moving the core template to the `ntn` engine, 2026-10-16 (30)

30. **The 2026-10-06 DSL changes the filter shapes, and makes its types
    non-global.** Porting the core template from the SDK runner to the `ntn`
    engine, typecheck rejected three things the SDK branch accepts:

    - Every property filter needs `type: "property"` (the discriminant for
      `type: "advanced"` groups).
    - Select, multi-select and status filters take an array:
      `value: ["Operations"]`, not `value: "Operations"`.
    - A `me` person filter is a one-element array:
      `value: [{ type: "relative", value: "me" }]`.

    The template's `types.d.ts` also exports its types instead of declaring
    them globally, so a build script can't name `PropertySchemaDefinition` or
    `ViewSchema` without an import, which build scripts can't have (finding
    29). `vendor/ntn-template/globals.d.ts` now re-declares those two as
    globals for the typecheck. The runtime doesn't need them.

    So a script written for one engine doesn't type-check on the other.
    Generated builds now get `"engine": "ntn"`.

    **✅ A one-member `and` group deploys as the view's saved filter.**
    `template-demo` was re-deployed on `ntn` with each team view's Team filter
    wrapped in a one-member `and` group. All 8 views now read
    `filter: {"property": …, "multi_select": {"contains": ["Operations"]}}`
    with `quick_filters: null`. Before, they read `filter: null` with the same
    condition under `quick_filters` (finding 21). The server flattens the
    group: the readback has no `and` wrapper. So finding 27's workaround
    works, and a script can now set a saved filter that isn't a removable
    pill. The API can't show whether a read-only member can change it, which
    is a UI check.

    Also on that run:

    - **An SDK-deployed build moves to `ntn` cleanly.** `ntn` read the SDK
      runner's `session.json`, created 0 resources, kept all 57 resource IDs
      unchanged, and rewrote the file in its own shape (finding 26) with the
      36 properties as `collection_property` entries. The compiled resourceIds
      are identical across the two engines (93 and 93). The build had no rows,
      so whether `ntn` re-deploys also clear relation values (finding 18) is
      untested.
    - **`me` filters still read back `null` on `ntn`.** My projects, My tasks
      and My meetings read `filter: null, quick_filters: null`, as on the SDK
      runner. Only the UI shows them. Untested: whether a `me` filter wrapped
      in an `and` group would read back under `filter`.

## From the template refinements deploy of 2026-10-16 (31–32)

`template-demo` re-deployed on `ntn` with new tabs (All projects, Active
projects, Open tasks), team pages mirroring every company tab, Docs "By type"
changed from board to table, and 17 sample rows with relation values. One
run, no errors: 17 pages created, and the 33 new view tabs mapped.

31. **A re-deploy ignores a change of view type, and the API can't change it
    either.** The company Docs "By type" view was deployed as a board and
    re-deployed as a table grouped by Type. It still reads `type: board`. The
    run reported nothing. `PATCH /v1/views/{id}` with `type: "table"` fails
    with `Configuration type "table" does not match view type "board"`. So a
    view's type only applies on create, like a teamspace's access level
    (finding 24). Fix it by hand in the UI (Layout → Table keeps the view's
    ID), or give the view a new resourceId, which leaves the old view in
    place.
32. **✅ On `ntn`, script-written relation values pair on both sides.** All
    sample relations were written on one side only (Tasks, Meeting Notes and
    Docs → Project, Meeting Notes → Action Items, Vendors → Projects), and
    every two-way one reads back from both sides: Projects shows Tasks 2/2/2,
    Meeting Notes 1/1/0 and Docs 2/0/0, matching the rows. That includes
    Tasks → Project, which read empty from the Tasks side on the SDK runner
    (findings 19 and 22). So on `ntn` a script can seed linked sample records
    on a first deploy. A re-deploy still clears them (finding 18, not
    retested).

Also confirmed on this run:

- **One-member `and` groups give a saved filter on a company database too.**
  "Active projects" (Status is In progress) reads under `filter`, with
  `quick_filters: null`.
- **Multi-member `and` groups stay groups.** Team "Active projects" and "Open
  tasks" read `filter: {and: [Team contains …, Status …]}`. Two
  `status_is_not` filters on one property inside one `and` group were
  accepted (cf. finding 17).
- **A `me` member drops out of the readback.** Team "My …" tabs read
  `filter: {and: [Team contains <team>]}`, with no person member. That's the
  same as the relative-date member missing in finding 25, so only the UI
  shows whether the `me` part landed.
- **The API can change a view's configuration, just not its type.**
  `PATCH /v1/views/{id}` accepted a board's `group_by` (status by `option`,
  `sort: ascending`) and card `properties` visibility, and kept the view's
  filter. The `configuration` must include `group_by` even when only
  `properties` changes, and a property left out of `properties` comes back
  hidden, including the title. The DSL has `statusBy: "option"` but no
  group sort.
- **A script-deployed timeline showed no rows until patched.** The company
  Projects Timeline showed nothing in the app, not even in its side table,
  though the rows had dates. Its config read back centred on
  2 January 2027 and, after the first patch, with
  `table_properties: [{property_id: "name"}]`, a property that doesn't
  exist. Re-centring (`preference.center_timestamp`) and setting
  `table_properties` to the real title and Dates IDs, then refreshing the
  app, fixed it. The cause isn't pinned down. A timeline created through the
  API on the same database worked straight away. The DSL has `tableProperties`
  but no centre or zoom.
- **Re-deploying adds tabs to an existing linked database.** Each team's
  linked databases kept their first tab's ID (renamed from the team name to
  "Board", "By date" and so on) and gained the new tabs.

## What works

Everything else deployed faithfully on the knoxx-rnd first run: two-way
relations, rollups (Total Hours = 18 on the seeded prawn project ✅),
status/select options with colors, auto-increment IDs (KIP-1…), filtered +
sorted views, calendar/timeline/board views, ephemeral views embedded as inline
linked databases on a hub page, column layouts, callouts, and child-page
placement.

- Do database automations work on a Plus workspace? (finding 9)
- Is finding 20 limited to `<mention-database>`, or are the other mention

  intentional, and will the spec be updated?

## Reading an existing build back out of Notion

The public API covers schema *and* views, though views are undocumented in the
SDK. `npm run pull -- --database=<id> --out=builds/<name>/source` wraps this:

```bash
curl -s "https://api.notion.com/v1/databases/$DB_ID"            -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTION_TOKEN" -H "Notion-Version: 2026-03-11"
curl -s "https://api.notion.com/v1/data_sources/$DS_ID"         -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTION_TOKEN" -H "Notion-Version: 2026-03-11"
curl -s "https://api.notion.com/v1/views?data_source_id=$DS_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTION_TOKEN" -H "Notion-Version: 2026-03-11"
curl -s "https://api.notion.com/v1/views/$VIEW_ID"              -H "Authorization: Bearer $NOTION_TOKEN" -H "Notion-Version: 2026-03-11"
```

Caveats: `GET /v1/views/{id}` 400s on feed views (35 of the CRM's 87), and
retrieved filters come back `null` wherever the filter uses a relative date or
the `me` variable — so "Today" / "My Meetings" views read as unfiltered.
Script-deployed filters also read `filter: null`, because they land in
`quick_filters` (finding 21), so check both fields.
